title: Navigation affordances and entropy guidelines (WIP)
content:
Purpose
Draft set of practical guidelines and wireframe notes for reducing navigation entropy in the Console. Focus is on sidebar affordances, route contracts (shallow vs deep), and lightweight patterns for handover and keyboard-first flows. This is a working doc: lots of sketchy thoughts, unanswered Qs, and backlog items.

Problem framing
- Current console nav feels noisy for users with 20+ projects and many model routes. People get lost between global-level actions (billing, org settings) and task-level surfaces (evals, model deployments).
- Observed behaviors in support tickets: users open multiple panes for the same task, search for hidden routes, or create duplicates of pages because deep links are ambiguous.
- Goal: reduce switch/scan time, make common tasks 1-2 interactions, and make fallbacks explicit when routes are missing or permissions differ.

Principles (high level)
- Anchor by task, not by object: surface the task entrypoint ("Create deployment", "Run eval") in a predictable global slot, then contextualize inside the workspace.
- Reduce branching entropy: prefer consistent affordances over many micro-variations. Keep the number of primary nav items to 6 (+ utility).
- Make routing contracts explicit: define when a route is stable for deep-linking vs when it is ephemeral (e.g., ephemeral run results).
- Keyboard-first and minimal mouse travel: provide stable focus anchors and single-key accelerators for primary tasks.

Sidebar affordance model (wireframe notes)
- Three-tier anatomy: Global rail (top), Context rail (middle), Task rail (bottom). Visual hierarchy via weight and spacing.
  - Global: org, billing, teams, admin. Icons + 1-line label on expanded, icons-only collapsed.
  - Context: workspace/project/model catalog. This is where users pick the object context. Clicking updates address bar context, but does not mutate active task.
  - Task: task entrypoints for the active context (train, deploy, eval, monitor). These are task anchors and should remain pinned while working, even if you navigate objects within the context.
- Compact vs expanded state handling: when collapsed, show badges (unread/errors) and hover tooltips with microcopy. On collapse->expand animation keep vertical anchor stable to avoid jumpiness.
- Flyout behavior: secondary, ephemeral pages (logs, quick-views) should open as right rail flyouts that do not change primary route. Deep link support for flyouts only when content is shareable (links can include flyout id param).

Routing semantics and examples
- Shallow route: /org/:orgId/projects/:projId/models -> safe to deep-link, stable for bookmarks.
- Task-route (stable anchor): /org/:orgId/projects/:projId/models/:modelId/deployments -> stable and canonical for primary tasks.
- Ephemeral route: /runs/:runId/trace -> ephemeral UI state; attempting to load without a run context should redirect to /runs and show a toast: "Run details not available — go to Runs list".
- Rule: deep links must resolve even when feature is behind a flag for that org: if the org lacks access, show a clear CTA to request access instead of 404.

Microcopy and affordance text examples
- Sidebar collapsed tooltip for "Deployments": "Deployments — active endpoints and scaling"
- Empty state for Task rail: "No deployments yet. Quickstart: Create a CPU deployment (1-2 mins) or try a sample model."
- Flyout header small helper: "Temporary view • Close to return to {task anchor}"

Keyboard-first behavior notes
- Stable anchors get single-letter shortcuts (g, p, d mapped to go-to, projects, deployments) with an overlay cheat-sheet on press. Shortcuts should be discoverable on first-run via a toast.
- Focus management: when opening a flyout, focus the first interactive control inside; Esc closes flyout and returns focus to previous anchor.

Wireframe sketches (descriptive)
- Desktop default: 64px-width rail with vertical stack: logo, global icons, divider, context list (collapsible), sticky task rail at bottom. Context items show small caret when they have tasks. Task rail uses grouped chips.
- Mobile/responsive: primary nav collapses behind hamburger; persistent bottom action bar with most-used tasks for the active context.

Backlog grooming (concrete tickets, prioritization)
- HIGH (MVP sprint):
  - CONSOLE-1840: implement three-tier sidebar skeleton + collapsed state (est 5d)
  - CONSOLE-1841: route-contracts spec + redirect behavior for ephemeral routes (est 2d)
  - CONSOLE-1842: keyboard shortcut overlay and first-run toast (est 3d)
- MEDIUM:
  - CONSOLE-1850: flyout deep-link support & shareable params (est 4d)
  - CONSOLE-1851: microcopy pass for task rail and empty states (content team) (est 2d)
- LOW:
  - CONSOLE-1860: analytics instrumentation to measure nav entropy (clicks-to-task, time-to-task) (est 3d)
  - CONSOLE-1861: mobile bottom action bar prototypes (design exploration) (est 5d)

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Sidebar skeleton renders consistently in collapsed/expanded states and preserves vertical anchor during toggle.
- Deep-linking for stable routes resolves for both normal and orgs without feature access (shows access CTA; does not 404).
- Keyboard overlay appears and shortcuts work for three primary anchors.

Open questions / TODOs
- How do we handle multiple active task anchors? Should we allow pinning more than one? (tradeoff: clutter vs multi-tasking)
- Permission surfaces: should the task rail hide actions the user cannot take or show them disabled with explanation? Initial bias: disable + explain so users learn available features.
- Performance: continuous nav updates for high-cardinality contexts (100+ models) — we need paging or typeahead; prototype with virtualized list.

Next steps
- Align with SRE on route redirect policies (Ravi)
- Quick prototype in Storybook: three-tier rail + keyboard overlay (Lucas)
- Microcopy draft pass and empty-state images (Maya)
- Kickoff grooming session with eng: target CX sprint for CONSOLE-1840

Notes-to-self
- collect examples from other consoles (notebook UX, cloud consoles) for "task rail" patterns
- consider A/B: hide task rail for teams < 3 daily actions

End of doc (WIP)
